rated_messages.input_message: You cant always control when you will see other people smoking. But you can control how you respond to your urge when you do.
When you begin to crave a cig, concentrate on your reasons for not smoking. Keep a list on your phone and look at it when you feel yourself beginning to falter.
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!
Practice going 10 minutes without smoking. Think of it just as practice. When the urge passes, reward yourself with a break from work or dinner from your favorite restaurant!

Think of urges as loud construction noises. Sometimes there's nothing you can do except agree that it's annoying. If you fight it, you feel more irritated, right? Let your urge be there until it passes on its own.
Seeing other people smoke is a predictable and unavoidable trigger. Take 5 slow, deep breaths and remind yourself that the urge will pass and that you do not need to smoke.
To help get through a 'risky situation', remind yourself of how far you've come and the effort that you've put in. Don't ruin your hard work - stay strong!
